headline_marked: [[Intel patent reveals XBM memory architecture]] to ease AI's memory bottleneck, ditches HBM's interposer
headline: Intel patent reveals XBM memory architecture to ease AI's memory bottleneck, ditches HBM's interposer
summary: Intel's Cross-Batch Memory (XBM) aims to match HBM4's footprint while using backend-transistor DRAM and UCIe links, potentially cutting costs and improving scalability.
details: An Intel patent application, filed in December 2024 and published July 2, 2026, details a new high-bandwidth memory (HBM) architecture called Cross-Batch Memory (XBM). This design aims to overcome the packaging and cost limitations of current interposer-based HBM solutions.

XBM proposes a memory stack built with back-end-of-line (BEOL) transistors and serial Universal Chiplet Interconnect Express (UCIe) links, replacing conventional DRAM and its ultra-wide interface. This approach seeks to match HBM4's footprint while reducing assembly costs.

The design features a stack of memory dies, each with 1.5GB (768 datablocks) of 1T1C DRAM fabricated in the BEOL. These dies are connected via through-silicon via (TSV) gutters and high-bandwidth interconnects, scaling from eight to 16 layers high.

Data exits the stack over UCIe I/O bundles at 32 gigatransfers per second (GT/s), routed through a base die to the compute die. This shift to a standard chiplet interconnect makes the design 'chiplet-native' and potentially simpler and cheaper to package than interposer-bound HBM stacks.

Intel's patent also emphasizes repairability, incorporating dedicated spare channels, built-in self-repair (BISR), and redundant memory arrays. These features are designed to improve yield on tall memory stacks by allowing post-assembly defect repair.

The patent also details memory-on-package (MoP) and 'reversed overhang' structures to reduce the stack's Z-height and eliminate the need for stiffeners. This contributes to the goal of a smaller, cheaper package for high-bandwidth memory.

While the patent was filed over 18 months ago, there is no further indication of ongoing development for XBM. This architecture is distinct from ZAM (Z-Angle Memory), another architecture Intel is co-developing with SAIMEMORY.

headline_marked: [[Samsung's chip division 2026 profit]] to exceed its past 40 years combined, eyes top spot
headline: Samsung's chip division 2026 profit to exceed its past 40 years combined, eyes top spot
summary: The Device Solutions (DS) unit's projected 2026 operating profit could reach $196 billion, potentially making Samsung the most profitable tech company for Q2.
details: Samsung Electronics' Device Solutions (DS) division is projected to achieve an operating profit in 2026 that will surpass its cumulative earnings over the past 40 years in the chip business. This staggering forecast was shared by DS president Kim Yong-Kwan with staff.

Brokerage consensus estimates Samsung's full-year 2026 operating profit near 300 trillion won ($196 billion). Its second-quarter figure is anticipated to be around 84.6 trillion won ($55.1 billion), which would exceed Nvidia's recent quarterly operating profit of $53.54 billion.

Should Samsung meet this Q2 mark, it would become the world's most profitable technology company for that period. The DS division alone contributed 53.7 trillion won ($35.1 billion) to Samsung's total operating profit in Q1 2026, representing about 94% of the company's overall earnings.

The record projection specifically applies to Samsung's memory and logic chip business, not the wider conglomerate, which includes smartphones and appliances. Samsung entered the semiconductor space in 1974 and shipped its first 64Kb DRAM in the mid-1980s.

The surge in profits is driven by robust AI server demand, which has outpaced supply, leading to steep increases in contract prices for DRAM and NAND. Memory makers are seeing 40% to 50% operating margins on NAND in the first half of the year.

Prices for 12 GB LPDDR5X modules have reached approximately $145, with further commodity DRAM increases being negotiated for Q3. Samsung has also informed customers to anticipate tight supply through at least 2027, indicating sustained high demand.
